content:
When Apple announced the Mac Studio equipped with the M5 Max chip yesterday, there was a pleasant surprise: the starting price remains unchanged from the M4 Max Mac Studio at US$2,499.

However, if you want to upgrade the GPU, there's a hidden catch in the upgrade cost — the actual cost will be US$300 more than the price initially shown on Apple's website…

Even John Gruber fell for this hidden upgrade fee, getting tripped up while mapping out the pricing for the various configurations of the newly announced machines yesterday.

The base configuration of this machine comes with an 18-core CPU and a 32-core GPU. Apple subsequently lists an option to upgrade to a 40-core GPU, clearly marked at an additional US$300.

The catch is that when you select this option, the memory is also automatically bumped from 32GB to 48GB, requiring an additional US$300. Since upgrading the GPU cores forces you to also upgrade to 48GB of memory, the actual upgrade cost is double the listed price — US$600.

Apple does hint at this in a slightly vague way when you select the chip upgrade.

Are you tempted to pick up one of the new Mac Mini or Mac Studio models? Let us know in the comments.
